prompt: Two endpoints have the same mean latency. One has many more very fast and very slow requests. Which quantity describes that added spread in the same units as latency?

options.explanation: It is the square root of variance and uses the original time units.
Equal means can accompany very different spreads.
Latency variance has squared time units, not milliseconds.
That has no role in measuring latency spread.

workedExample: First identify the property: variation of individual observations about their centre. Variance quantifies squared deviations; its square root gives a spread measure back in time units.

prompt: Two correlated quantities have finite second moments. Which statements hold without an additional independence or zero-covariance assumption? Select all that apply.

options.text: Scaling and shifting one quantity scales and shifts its expectation.
The variance of their sum is always the sum of variances.
options.explanation: Covariance contributes to spread of a sum.

options.text: The mean of their product always equals the product of means.
options.explanation: That equality needs zero covariance in this finite-second-moment setting.

options.text: The expected total is the sum of their expectations.
options.explanation: Linearity holds for finite expectations regardless of dependence.

workedExample: Separate means of linear combinations from products and spread. Dependence changes how quantities move together, but does not invalidate adding their finite expected contributions.
